nodes.description: Inbred 129 substrain mice carry a naturally occurring SUGCT deficiency that produces a GA3 urinary trait. Crossing it onto the GA1 mouse lowered 3-hydroxyglutarate and glutarylcarnitine, showing SUGCT supplies glutaryl-CoA in vivo.

evidence.reference_title: Glutaric aciduria type 3 is a naturally occurring biochemical trait in inbred mice of 129 substrains.
evidence.snippet: We found that GA1 mice with SUGCT deficiency have decreased excretion of urine 3-hydroxyglutaric acid and decreased levels glutarylcarnitine in urine, plasma and kidney.

nodes.description: No treatment is established or generally required. In a single symptomatic child with cyclic vomiting, an antibiotic trial intended to reduce intestinal bacterial glutaric acid production was followed by significant clinical improvement. This is an uncontrolled single-case observation.
nodes.id: Antibiotic trial to reduce bacterial glutarate production

evidence.reference_title: Glutaric Aciduria Type 3: Three Unrelated Canadian Cases, with Different Routes of Ascertainment.
evidence.snippet: A trial of antibiotic treatment, to minimise bacterial GA production, was followed by significant clinical improvement.

nodes.description: Recurrent or cyclic vomiting and other gastrointestinal disturbance have been described in a minority of patients. Attribution to GA3 is unproven; most reported patients have no gastrointestinal symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Glutaric Aciduria Type 3: Three Unrelated Canadian Cases, with Different Routes of Ascertainment.
evidence.snippet: In one of our patients, severe episodes of cyclic vomiting were the major problem.

evidence.reference_title: Glutaric aciduria type III: a distinctive non-disease?
evidence.snippet: The second boy suffered from acute gastroenteritis and hyperthyroidism, when an excessively high urinary glutaric acid excretion was identified (1460 mmol/mol creatinine).

nodes.description: Glutaric acid that cannot be re-esterified accumulates and is excreted, giving persistent isolated glutaric aciduria with low 3-hydroxyglutarate. Reported urinary glutarate ranges from tens to over a thousand mmol/mol creatinine. Unlike glutaric aciduria type 1, no glutaryl-CoA or 3-hydroxyglutarate build-up occurs, so the neurotoxic metabolites of GA1 are not expected.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic mapping of glutaric aciduria, type 3, to chromosome 7 and identification of mutations in c7orf10.
evidence.snippet: we found three healthy children who excreted abnormal quantities of glutaric acid but low 3-hydroxyglutaric acid, a pattern consistent with glutaric aciduria type 3 (GA3).

nodes.description: Persistent isolated excretion of glutaric acid with a raised ratio of glutarate to 3-hydroxyglutarate, glutarylcarnitine and glutarylglycine. It is the defining and frequently the only finding.

evidence.reference_title: Glutaric aciduria type III: a distinctive non-disease?
evidence.snippet: Glutaric aciduria type III is a rare metabolic abnormality leading to persistent isolated glutaric acid excretion.

evidence.reference_title: Glutaric Aciduria Type 3: Three Unrelated Canadian Cases, with Different Routes of Ascertainment.
evidence.snippet: Glutaric aciduria type 3 (GA3) is associated with decreased conversion of free glutaric acid to glutaryl-coA, reflecting deficiency of succinate-hydroxymethylglutarate coA-transferase, caused by variants in the SUGCT (C7orf10) gene.

nodes.description: Intestinal bacteria produce glutaric acid, and this contributes to the glutarate load in SUGCT deficiency. In SUGCT-knockout mice, antibiotic depletion of the gut flora returned metabolite levels to wild-type, and in one patient an antibiotic trial aimed at reducing bacterial glutarate production was followed by clinical improvement.

evidence.reference_title: Knockout of the non-essential gene SUGCT creates diet-linked, age-related microbiome disbalance with a diabetes-like metabolic syndrome phenotype.
evidence.snippet: After SugctKO mice were treated with antibiotics, metabolites were comparable to WT, indicating that the microbiome affects metabolism in SugctKO mice.

nodes.description: SUGCT performs a metabolite-repair reaction: it returns free glutarate to glutaryl-CoA so it can be oxidised by glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase. When the reaction fails, glutarate becomes a dead-end metabolite, and the glutaryl-CoA-derived products fall relative to glutarate. The enzyme is most highly expressed in kidney and liver.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization, Structure, and Inhibition of the Human Succinyl-CoA:glutarate-CoA Transferase, a Putative Genetic Modifier of Glutaric Aciduria Type 1.
evidence.snippet: Since glutaric acid would otherwise be a dead-end metabolite excreted in urine, this process is viewed as an example of metabolite repair.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization, Structure, and Inhibition of the Human Succinyl-CoA:glutarate-CoA Transferase, a Putative Genetic Modifier of Glutaric Aciduria Type 1.
evidence.snippet: Expression of SUGCT is not uniform, with high mRNA levels in kidney and liver.

evidence.reference_title: Glutaric aciduria type 3 is a naturally occurring biochemical trait in inbred mice of 129 substrains.
evidence.snippet: Our work demonstrates that SUGCT contributes to the production of glutaryl-CoA under conditions of low and pathologically high glutaric acid levels.

nodes.description: Free glutarate arises as a side product of the mitochondrial lysine and tryptophan degradation pathway, thought to come from hydrolysis of glutaryl-CoA. Its production therefore scales with the load of the precursor amino acids.

evidence.reference_title: C7orf10 encodes succinate-hydroxymethylglutarate CoA-transferase, the enzyme that converts glutarate to glutaryl-CoA.
evidence.snippet: Glutarate, a side-product in the metabolism of tryptophan and lysine, is metabolized by conversion to glutaryl-CoA by a transferase using succinyl-CoA as a coenzyme donor.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic mapping of glutaric aciduria, type 3, to chromosome 7 and identification of mutations in c7orf10.
evidence.snippet: Direct sequencing of C7orf10 revealed that the three Amish individuals were homozygous for a nonsynonymous sequence variant (c.895C-->T, Arg299Trp).

evidence.reference_title: Two patients with glutaric aciduria type 3: a novel mutation and brain magnetic resonance imaging findings.
evidence.snippet: One of our patients had a homozygous mutation p.Arg322Trp (c.964C > T) of SUGCT (NM_001193311) gene.

evidence.reference_title: A Rare Contiguous Gene Deletion Leading to Trichothiodystrophy Type 4 and Glutaric Aciduria Type 3.
evidence.snippet: Microarray analysis revealed a homozygous microdeletion involving the MPLKIP and SUGCT genes, which are located close to each other.

evidence.reference_title: Case report: Paternal uniparental disomy on chromosome 7 and homozygous SUGCT mutation in a fetus with overweight after birth.
evidence.snippet: Whole exome and Sanger sequencing revealed a homozygous frameshift mutation in SUGCT at 7p14.1, from the heterozygous carrier father, with no contribution from the mother.

nodes.description: Biallelic SUGCT variants abolish succinyl-CoA:glutarate-CoA transferase activity. The recurrent missense allele (reported as p.Arg299Trp in the original Amish study and as p.Arg336Trp in the functional study, a difference of transcript numbering) yields insoluble, inactive protein; nonsense alleles, a frameshift, and homozygous contiguous deletions of SUGCT with the neighbouring MPLKIP gene have also been reported.

animal_models.description: The knockout removes SUGCT, the primary lesion of GA3, and was made to study the disease mechanism.
animal_models.name: Sugct knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: C7orf10 encodes succinate-hydroxymethylglutarate CoA-transferase, the enzyme that converts glutarate to glutaryl-CoA.
evidence.snippet: The p.Arg336Trp mutation led to the production of insoluble and inactive C7orf10 both in Escherichia coli and in HEK293T cells.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic mapping of glutaric aciduria, type 3, to chromosome 7 and identification of mutations in c7orf10.
evidence.snippet: We then sequenced three non-Amish children with GA3 and discovered two nonsense mutations (c.322C-->T, Arg108Ter, and c.424C-->T, Arg142Ter) in addition to the Amish mutation.

evidence.reference_title: Novel contiguous gene deletion in peruvian girl with Trichothiodystrophy type 4 and glutaric aciduria type 3.
evidence.snippet: Chromosome microarray analysis showed a 125 kb homozygous pathogenic deletion, which includes genes MPLKIP and SUGCT, not described before.

nodes.description: Sugct knockout mice show imbalanced kidney lipid and acylcarnitine metabolism and gut microbiome changes, with age-dependent kidney, liver and adipose pathology and an obesity-related phenotype that a high-lysine diet accelerates. The human counterparts of these findings have not been reported.

evidence.reference_title: Knockout of the non-essential gene SUGCT creates diet-linked, age-related microbiome disbalance with a diabetes-like metabolic syndrome phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we show that the SugctKO kidney pathology is accelerated and exacerbated by a high-lysine diet.
